spec.title: Does raising the minimum wage cost jobs? Card and Krueger found fast-food jobs rose 2.76 in New Jersey
spec.statement: Card and Krueger (American Economic Review, 1994) compared fast-food restaurants in New Jersey, which raised its minimum wage in 1992, with those in eastern Pennsylvania, which didn't. They report that employment per store rose by 2.76 full-time equivalents in New Jersey relative to Pennsylvania. This runs an independent rebuild on the authors' public survey data. The rebuild isn't the authors' code, so a mismatch ends as inconclusive.

source.authors: D. Card, A. B. Krueger; rebuild by GitHub user laibabasraa-ux
